title: Bolt.new: How we scaled $0-20m ARR in 60 days, with 15 people — Eric Simons, Bolt
talk_summary: Eric Simons recounts how Bolt.new went from $0.7M to $20M ARR in ~60 days with under 20 people, emphasizing tiny high-context teams, ruthless prioritization, and AI-assisted support.

takeaways.technique: Fire-truck triage: explicitly choose which fires burn
takeaways.what_they_do: When everything is on fire, they pick the highest-impact infrastructure and key people to save and consciously let other fires burn, rather than trying to cover everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there are some fires that are just going to have to burn and that's okay

takeaways.technique: Small number of high-context agents with agency
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately keep headcount low so each person has more context and can act without permission chains, which they credit for speed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you really want a small number of people with more context per head
takeaways.numbers: under 20 people, ~30-40k active customers at month two

takeaways.technique: AI support deflection with a dedicated tool
takeaways.what_they_do: They deployed an AI support assistant (Parella/SAM) that auto-resolves most inbound tickets, replacing what would have been a large human support team.
takeaways.evidence_quote: takes out 90% of our tickets automatically
takeaways.numbers: ~90% of tickets auto-resolved; would have needed ~50 people a year or two earlier

takeaways.technique: Weekly public office hours to smooth churn
takeaways.what_they_do: They ran weekly live sessions showing what they were building and answering questions, to keep users believing during a brittle MVP period.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we started running a a weekly office hour session

takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly discount prevailing industry advice (remote work, headcount, fundraising) and make decisions from their own assessment of reality.
takeaways.evidence_quote: think for yourself and don't just adopt a lot of the hive mind stuff
